## Reykjavík Weather-Ready 2-Day Plan
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg

A budget-friendly city break for **2 adults** with a **$250 total target** is most realistic with mostly walking, one or two paid indoor stops, and simple meals. In early March, Reykjavík is often **cold, windy, and changeable**, so this plan keeps outdoor time flexible and adds indoor backups.

## 2-Day Reykjavík Itinerary for 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-11
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg

| Day | Plan | Indoor fallback | Est. cost for 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mar 10 | Downtown walk, Hallgrímskirkja area, Harpa exterior, Old Harbour, sunset by the waterfront | Reykjavík Art Museum or National Museum | $40–$85 |
| Mar 11 | Perlan area, city viewpoints, geothermal pool, café time, souvenir stroll | Perlan exhibits and café, then a longer museum stop | $55–$110 |

### Day 1: Downtown Reykjavík and the Harbor
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Start in the city center near **Laugavegur** and **Austurvöllur** for an easy first walk.
- Midday: Visit the **Hallgrímskirkja** area and continue to **Harpa** for architecture and harbor views.
- Afternoon: Walk the **Old Harbour** and keep the route short if it is windy.
- Evening: Choose a casual dinner near downtown; aim for soup, pizza, or a bowl-style meal to stay on budget.
- Indoor alternative: If it is cold or snowy, swap the harbor walk for **Reykjavík Art Museum** or a longer café stop.
- Budget target: **$20–$40 per person** if you keep attractions free and eat simply.

Action: [Button: View city map](https://www.visitreykjavik.is/)

### Day 2: Perlan, Pools, and Warm-Up Stops
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- Morning: Head to the **Perlan** area for viewpoints and a weather-safe indoor start.
- Midday: Add a geothermal pool stop if conditions feel harsh; this is one of the best winter-friendly Reykjavík experiences.
- Afternoon: Spend time in a museum, souvenir shop, or a relaxed café depending on wind and visibility.
- Evening: Keep dinner simple and close to your lodging to avoid extra transport costs.
- Indoor alternative: If it is snowy or very windy, make this a mostly indoor day with **Perlan + museum + café**.
- Budget target: **$25–$55 per person**, depending on museum/pool choices.

Action: [Button: Plan indoor stops](https://www.visitreykjavik.is/)

## Weather-Smart Clothing to Pack
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/snow.svg

- **Base layer:** thermal top and leggings
- **Mid layer:** fleece or light sweater
- **Outer layer:** waterproof, windproof jacket
- **Bottoms:** warm trousers; add thermal leggings if you run cold
- **Footwear:** waterproof walking shoes or boots with good grip
- **Accessories:** hat, gloves, scarf/neck gaiter, wool socks
- **Useful extras:** compact umbrella is less helpful than a hood in Reykjavík wind; bring a small daypack for layers

## Budget Fit for Two Adults
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-rupee.svg

- **Lowest-friction version:** mostly free walking + 1 paid indoor stop + casual meals
- **Likely total:** about **$140–$250** for two adults over 2 days
- **Best savings moves:** use walking, choose one paid attraction per day, and eat soup, bakery items, or casual plates instead of sit-down dinners
